What is SchoolAI?

Classroom-first AI platform built around monitored 'Spaces' - teacher-created AI experiences that students enter, with the teacher seeing every conversation live and receiving safety alerts. Includes Dot, a student companion, and Sidekick for teachers.

Best for

Giving students direct AI access with real-time teacher supervision.

Main features

  • Spaces (teacher-designed AI activities with defined objectives)
  • live teacher dashboard showing every student conversation in real time
  • automated safety and wellbeing alerts escalated to staff
  • Dot student companion that adapts to each learner
  • Sidekick teacher assistant
  • historical character simulations
  • standards alignment
  • district admin controls.

Practical use cases

  • Letting a whole class interview a historical figure safely
  • running a differentiated practice activity with live teacher visibility
  • flagging a student in distress through content alerts
  • teacher lesson prep.

Who is it for?

  • K-12 teachers, school leaders and districts wanting supervised student AI access.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium for teachers; per-student district licensing

Plans described in the source

Free tier for individual teachers with limited Spaces and student seats. Paid teacher tier roughly $10-15/mo. School and district licensing quoted per student per year (commonly in the $8-20 per student range depending on scale and modules). Verify with sales - district pricing is negotiated.

Free plan

Yes - free teacher tier with limited Spaces and students.

Free trial

School pilots offered through sales; free tier serves individual teachers.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier limits the number of active Spaces and concurrent students. Full analytics, SSO and rostering require a paid school plan.

Confirm current plans and pricing ↗

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The live monitoring dashboard is the strongest student-safety implementation in this category - teachers see every message as it happens
  • wellbeing alerts have real duty-of-care value
  • Spaces give structure that open chat lacks
  • rostering integrations are solid.

Limitations to consider

  • Less breadth of teacher-productivity tools than MagicSchool
  • requires teacher setup time to design good Spaces
  • per-student pricing gets expensive at district scale
  • younger company with a shorter track record
  • US-centric.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • Google Classroom and Clever/ClassLink rostering

Languages

  • Multilingual output; interface primarily English

API access

Enterprise integrations rather than a public API

Integrations and exports

  • Google Classroom, Clever, ClassLink, Canvas, Google Workspace for Education, Microsoft 365 Education

Evaluation notes

The safety-alert system is the reason districts buy this rather than a general chatbot. Review the alert escalation workflow and data-retention policy carefully during procurement.
